questions.question: The ________ Polo Club is the home of the Ezra Cup event, the world's oldest polo tournament, started in 1880.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ezra Cup is recognized as the **world's oldest polo tournament**, initiated in 1880.
 
• The tournament is hosted by the **Calcutta Polo Club**, which is also the oldest polo club globally, established in 1862.
 
• The Calcutta Polo Club played a crucial role in popularizing polo internationally and preserving its legacy.
 
• Ezra Cup is named after **David Elias Ezra**, a Jewish businessperson and patron of polo in Kolkata.
 
• This prestigious tournament continues to attract players and enthusiasts from around the world, celebrating the sport's rich heritage in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polo Origins:**

 
 
• Polo originated in ancient Persia around 2,500 years ago and was initially a training game for cavalry units.
 
• The modern version of polo was formalized by British tea planters in India during the 19th century.
 
• The game involves teams competing to score by driving a ball into the opposing team's goal using mallets.
 
 
 
• **Calcutta Polo Club:**
 
 
• Founded in 1862, the Calcutta Polo Club is considered the oldest in existence worldwide.
 
• It has significantly contributed to promoting polo and nurturing talent in India and beyond.
 
• The club is located in Kolkata, West Bengal, India.
 
 
 
• **David Elias Ezra:**
 
 
• A prominent Jewish businessman who contributed to Kolkata's development in various domains.
 
• He was a key patron of the Calcutta Polo Club and played a vital role in establishing the Ezra Cup.
 
 
 
• **Polo in India:**
 
 
• India has a rich legacy in polo, with the sport flourishing during the British colonial era.
 
• The Indian Army remains one of the major contributors to polo's development and popularity in the country.
 
• India hosts several significant polo tournaments annually, including the Ezra Cup.

questions.question: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) envisaged by the Central Government is called ____________:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mission Karmayogi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mission Karmayogi** is the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) launched by the Government of India.
 
• The initiative aims to transform civil services by focusing on **capacity building, professional development, and skill enhancement** of government officials.
 
• It was **approved by the Union Cabinet** on September 2, 2020, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• This program emphasizes the creation of a **competency-driven civil service ecosystem** through digital platforms and training modules.
 
• Mission Karmayogi is implemented through the **Integrated Government Online Training (iGOT 2.0) digital platform**, offering continuous learning opportunities for civil servants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integrated Government Online Training (iGOT 2.0)**:

 
 
• It is the digital learning platform under Mission Karmayogi designed for civil servants.
 
• iGOT 2.0 offers personalized and competency-based learning modules for professional development.
 
 
 
• **Capacity Building Commission (CBC)**:
 
 
• Established under Mission Karmayogi to oversee training methodologies and capacity-building standards.
 
• CBC ensures alignment with institutional goals and provides guidance to training institutes.
 
 
 
• **Institutional Framework**:
 
 
• Mission Karmayogi is governed by the Prime Minister's Public Human Resources Council.
 
• The council provides strategic direction and monitors program implementation.
 
 
 
• **Objective**:
 
 
• To develop a future-ready civil service equipped with modern skills, ethical values, and citizen-centric governance principles.
 
• Focuses on fostering collaboration across departments and ministries.

questions.question: In a food chain of Algae-Shrimp-Fish-Bird, if the energy available at the bird is 4 kJ, then the energy available at the shrimp is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (400 kJ)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a food chain, energy transfer follows the **10% rule**, where only 10% of energy is passed to the next trophic level, while the rest is lost as heat, respiration, or other processes.
 
• The energy available at the bird is 4 kJ. Using the 10% rule, the energy at the fish would be 40 kJ, at the shrimp 400 kJ, and at the algae 4000 kJ.
 
• **Shrimp represents the second trophic level** in the given food chain, and its energy level is calculated by considering the energy available to subsequent levels.
 
• The correct energy available at shrimp is **400 kJ**, derived by sequentially applying the 10% rule for energy transfer across trophic levels.
 
• This calculation assumes the energy transfer process is consistent across all levels and aligns with the principles of ecological energy flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels:** These are hierarchical levels in a food chain, including producers (e.g., algae), primary consumers (e.g., shrimp), secondary consumers (e.g., fish), and tertiary consumers (e.g., birds).
 
• **10% Rule:** A fundamental concept in ecology stating that approximately 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, while 90% is lost to the environment.
 
• **Energy Pyramid:** A graphical representation showing the energy flow in an ecosystem, where energy decreases as we move up the pyramid due to inefficiencies in energy transfer.
 
• **Primary Producers:** Organisms like algae that produce energy through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.
 
• **Ecological Efficiency:** The efficiency of energy transfer between trophic levels, typically low due to energy losses such as heat and metabolic processes.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian Female Dancer to receive the highest Padma award, Padma Vibhushan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonal Mansingh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sonal Mansingh** is the first Indian female dancer to be honored with the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, in the field of art.
 
• She received this award in the year **1992** for her outstanding contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Mansingh is a renowned exponent of **Odissi** and **Bharatanatyam**, two of India's most celebrated classical dance forms.
 
• She is also known for her innovative choreographies that address contemporary social issues, blending traditional and modern themes.
 
• In addition to the Padma Vibhushan, she has also been awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in 2003 and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian awards in India, comprising three categories: **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri**.
 
• They are awarded in various disciplines such as art, literature, social work, public affairs, science, and sports.
 
• **Padma Vibhushan** is the second-highest civilian award, given for "exceptional and distinguished service."
 
 
 
• **Odissi Dance:**
 
 
• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, intricate footwork, and sculpturesque poses inspired by temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam Dance:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate hand gestures, and facial expressions.
 
• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, with roots in Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, established in 1953.
 
• It presents awards to artists for their outstanding contributions to Indian performing arts.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, but they are not enforceable by any court. This concept is mentioned in which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 37**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 37 of the Indian Constitution explicitly states that Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are fundamental to the governance of the country.
 
• While DPSPs are not enforceable by any court, they serve as guiding principles for the state to frame policies and laws.
 
• The purpose of Article 37 is to ensure that DPSPs are treated as goals for the government to achieve, promoting social justice and welfare.
 
• Article 37 clarifies the non-justiciable nature of DPSPs, differentiating them from Fundamental Rights which are enforceable by courts.
 
• DPSPs aim to establish a welfare state by providing a framework for addressing issues like education, health, economic equality, and social security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51) deals with DPSPs.
 
• These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to promote socio-economic development.
 
• DPSPs include provisions for promoting equal pay, improving public health, protecting the environment, and providing free legal aid.
 
• They act as guidelines for lawmakers to create policies that ensure the welfare of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Difference between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are non-justiciable.
 
• Fundamental Rights ensure individual freedoms, whereas DPSPs focus on collective welfare and governance.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 37:**
 
 
• Serves as a bridge between the ideals of governance and practical policymaking.
 
• Encourages the state to work toward achieving socio-economic objectives outlined in DPSPs.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation of DPSPs:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India has emphasized the harmonious construction of Fundamental Rights and DPSPs to achieve constitutional goals.
 
• In landmark cases like Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, DPSPs were recognized as essential for building a welfare state.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is played by Shreya Bhattacharjee, an eminent musician from Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tabla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shreya Bhattacharjee is a renowned musician from Assam known for her expertise in playing the **Tabla**.
 
• She started her journey in music at a young age and has achieved remarkable recognition in the field of Indian classical music.
 
• Shreya has won numerous awards and accolades for her exceptional Tabla performances at national and international levels.
 
• She has contributed significantly to promoting Indian classical percussion instruments, especially among the younger generation.
 
• Her mastery over intricate rhythms and patterns makes her a celebrated artist in the world of classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla:**

 
 
• The Tabla is a pair of twin hand-played drums used in Indian classical music and other genres.
 
• It comprises two drums – the **Dayan** (right drum, smaller, wooden) and the **Bayan** (left drum, larger, metal or clay).
 
• The instrument is known for its ability to produce intricate rhythms and tonal variations.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music:**
 
 
• Indian classical music has two major traditions – Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• The Tabla is a prominent percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
 
 
• **Famous Tabla Players:**
 
 
• Legendary artists like Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Kishan Maharaj have popularized the Tabla globally.
 
 
 
• **Rhythm in Music:**
 
 
• In Indian classical music, rhythms are structured into cycles called **Tala**, which serve as the foundation for compositions and improvisation.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory from the following has the highest sex ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, Puducherry recorded the highest sex ratio among Union Territories, with **1,037 females per 1,000 males**.
 
• Puducherry's sex ratio is significantly higher than the national average of 940 females per 1,000 males, as per the same census.
 
• The union territory consists of four districts: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam, collectively contributing to the high sex ratio.
 
• The government of Puducherry has focused on enhancing healthcare facilities and gender equality, contributing to the improved sex ratio.
 
• Among other Union Territories, Lakshadweep follows Puducherry with a sex ratio of 946 females per 1,000 males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio Definition:** It refers to the number of females per 1,000 males in a given population and is an important demographic indicator.
 
• **National Average (2011):** The sex ratio in India as per the 2011 Census stands at 940 females per 1,000 males.
 
• **Factors Influencing Sex Ratio:** Various factors, including access to healthcare, education, gender equality, and cultural practices, impact the sex ratio.
 
• **Puducherry's Policies:** Initiatives like maternal healthcare programs and women empowerment schemes have contributed to its favorable sex ratio.
 
• **Global Perspective:** The sex ratio varies widely across countries, and India has been working towards improving its gender balance through multiple policy measures.

questions.question: 'Waiting for a Visa' is a 20-page autobiography of ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **"Waiting for a Visa"** is a 20-page autobiography written by **Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar**, one of India's most eminent social reformers.
 
• This autobiography was written between **1935 and 1936**, and it serves as a personal account of Dr Ambedkar's experiences with caste-based discrimination.
 
• The work is considered an **educational document** and is part of the Columbia University syllabus for its insights into social issues.
 
• It highlights the challenges faced by marginalized communities in pre-independence India and Dr Ambedkar’s efforts to combat social injustice.
 
• Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar is also known as the **architect of the Indian Constitution** and the leader of the Dalit movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar:**

 
 
• He was born on **14 April 1891** in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, and belonged to the Mahar caste, a Dalit community.
 
• He earned a doctorate from **Columbia University** and a D.Sc. from the London School of Economics.
 
• He played a pivotal role in drafting the **Constitution of India** and was the first Law Minister of independent India.
 
• Ambedkar converted to Buddhism in 1956, along with millions of his followers, as a rejection of caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Significance of "Waiting for a Visa":**
 
 
• The book is a firsthand account of casteism in India and provides insights into the social fabric of that time.
 
• It is a valuable resource for understanding the plight of Dalits and the systemic discrimination they faced.
 
• The narrative is both autobiographical and a call for social reform.
 
 
 
• **Dr Ambedkar’s Contributions:**
 
 
• He fought for the rights of the untouchables and worked to abolish the caste system.
 
• He founded the **Independent Labour Party** in 1936 and later the **Scheduled Castes Federation**.
 
• He was instrumental in the formation of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) based on his economic thesis.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Dr Ambedkar is celebrated annually on **Ambedkar Jayanti**, observed on 14th April.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in 1990.
 
• His writings and speeches continue to inspire movements for social justice and equality worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following Commissions was set up to investigate the incident of Jallianwala Bagh in 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hunter Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hunter Commission was established in **October 1919** by the British government to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre that occurred on April 13, 1919.
 
• The commission was chaired by **Lord William Hunter**, a British lawyer and former Solicitor-General of Scotland.
 
• It consisted of seven members, including **four British officials** and **three Indian members**.
 
• The commission's primary aim was to examine the **actions of General Reginald Dyer**, who ordered troops to open fire on unarmed civilians gathered at Jallianwala Bagh.
 
• The Hunter Commission condemned Dyer’s actions but failed to recommend stringent punishment, leading to widespread criticism among Indians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Name the Union territory with the lowest density of population as per Census of India 2011.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have the **lowest population density** among Union Territories in India, according to the Census 2011.
 
• The population density of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is **46 persons per square kilometer**, which is significantly lower than other Union Territories.
 
• This Union Territory consists of **572 islands**, with only a few being inhabited, contributing to its low population density.
 
• The region has dense forest cover, with forests occupying about **86% of the total area**, leaving limited land for human habitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:** It refers to the number of people living per unit of area, typically measured as persons per square kilometer.
 
• **Census 2011:** The Census of India is conducted every 10 years, and the 2011 Census was the 15th National Census since 1872.
 
• **Union Territories of India:** These are administrative divisions governed directly by the Central Government. There are currently 8 Union Territories in India.
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:** A Union Territory of India located in the Bay of Bengal, known for its rich biodiversity and indigenous tribal communities.
 
• **Forest Cover:** The extensive forest cover in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands plays a key role in maintaining ecological balance but limits the extent of human settlement.

questions.question: Which of the following is an artificial port in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chennai port**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chennai Port** is an artificial and one of the largest ports in India, located in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is the **second largest port in India** in terms of cargo handling and is known for its modern infrastructure.
 
• Originally called **Madras Port**, it is the oldest artificial port on the East Coast of India.
 
• The port was established in the 19th century and continues to play a major role in India's maritime trade.
 
• It primarily handles a wide range of cargo, including containers, automobiles, and liquid cargo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Port:** A port constructed by human intervention, as opposed to natural harbors that form naturally along coastlines.
 
• **Natural Ports in India:** Examples include Mumbai Port, Marmagao Port, and Cochin Port, which are located in naturally sheltered areas.
 
• **Chennai Port’s Connectivity:** It is well-connected to inland areas via railways and roadways, making it a key trade hub in South India.
 
• **Deendayal Port:** Located in Gujarat, it is a natural port, formerly known as Kandla Port, and plays a significant role in India's trade.
 
• **Kolkata Port:** Though an important port, it is a riverine port and not an artificial one like Chennai Port.

questions.question: In Maikal hills, which of the following minerals is deposited?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bauxite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maikal Hills, part of the Satpura Range, are located in the Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh region of India.
 
• This region is rich in mineral resources, with **bauxite** being one of the primary deposits.
 
• Bauxite is the chief ore of aluminum, making it a critical mineral for the manufacturing of aluminum products.
 
• The mineral reserves in the Maikal Hills contribute to India's significant bauxite production, which ranks among the top in the world.
 
• Bauxite mining in this region supports industries such as aluminum smelting and alumina refining.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bauxite Composition:** Bauxite is primarily composed of aluminum hydroxide minerals like gibbsite, boehmite, and diaspore, along with impurities such as iron oxides and silica.
 
• **Uses of Bauxite:** It is mainly used in aluminum production, but also finds applications in the manufacturing of refractory materials, abrasives, and cement.
 
• **Global Production:** India is one of the leading bauxite producers globally, with other major contributors being Australia, Guinea, and China.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Bauxite mining can lead to deforestation, habitat destruction, and soil erosion, which necessitates sustainable mining practices.
 
• **Aluminum Industry:** Aluminum derived from bauxite is used extensively in transportation, construction, packaging, and electrical industries due to its lightweight and corrosion-resistant properties.

questions.question: Which of the following possesses the largest isolated single cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ostrich egg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **ostrich egg** is the largest isolated single cell in nature, with an average weight of around 1.4 kg and a diameter of approximately 15–18 cm.
 
• It is classified as a single cell because it contains the female ostrich's ovum, making it a reproductive cell (gamete).
 
• The shell of the ostrich egg is strong and thick, measuring about 2–4 mm in thickness, to support its large size and protect it from external damage.
 
• Despite its size, the ostrich egg is relatively small compared to the body size of the ostrich, which is the largest bird in the world.
 
• It takes about 42 days for an ostrich egg to hatch, and it can withstand a weight of up to 120 kg without breaking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Definition:** A cell is the basic unit of life in all living organisms. In the case of an ostrich egg, the entire egg (excluding the shell) is a single cell with a nucleus.
 
• **Gametes:** These are reproductive cells that unite during fertilization to form a new organism. The ostrich egg is the female gamete, while the sperm is the male gamete.
 
• **Largest Animal Cells:** In addition to the ostrich egg, other large cells in the animal kingdom include certain types of neurons in whales and squids.
 
• **Blue Whale and Amoeba:** While the blue whale is the largest animal, its cells are not unusually large. Amoeba, though a single-celled organism, is much smaller than an ostrich egg.
 
• **Structural Support:** The ostrich egg’s shell is made of calcium carbonate, providing protection and structural integrity, essential for embryonic development.

questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) of a body which accelerates from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 2 seconds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5 m/sec²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Acceleration is calculated using the formula: **a = (v - u) / t**, where:

 
 
• **v** = final velocity
 
• **u** = initial velocity
 
• **t** = time taken
 
 
 
• Given:
 
 
• Initial velocity, **u = 5 m/s**
 
• Final velocity, **v = 10 m/s**
 
• Time taken, **t = 2 seconds**
 
 
 
• Substitute the values into the formula: **a = (10 - 5) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 m/sec²**.
 
• Hence, the acceleration of the body is **2.5 m/sec²**.
 
• This calculation aligns with the laws of motion as defined by Sir Isaac Newton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration:** It is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time. Its SI unit is **m/s²**.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** When an object's velocity changes at a constant rate over time, it is said to experience uniform acceleration.
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (**F = ma**).
 
• **Velocity:** It refers to the rate of change of displacement of an object with respect to time and has both magnitude and direction.
 
• **SI Units:** The International System of Units (SI) standardizes physical measurements, where:
 
 
• Velocity is measured in **m/s**.
 
• Time is measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
• Acceleration is measured in **m/s²**.

questions.question: Who presides over the House in absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker in the Indian political system?

options.text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chairperson so nominated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Indian parliamentary system, when both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are absent, a **member appointed by the Speaker** presides over the proceedings.
 
• The Chairperson so nominated is selected from among the members of the Lok Sabha and performs the Speaker's duties temporarily.
 
• This arrangement ensures the smooth functioning of the House during unforeseen absences of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
 
• The role of the Chairperson so nominated is limited to presiding over sessions and does not extend to full powers of the Speaker.
 
• Such provisions are laid out in the **Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha** to maintain parliamentary decorum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:** The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha and is responsible for maintaining order and decorum in the House.
 
• **Deputy Speaker:** The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha members and acts as the presiding officer in the absence of the Speaker.
 
• **Rules of Procedure:** These rules govern the functioning of the Lok Sabha and include provisions for temporary presiding officers.
 
• **Parliamentary Decorum:** The presiding officer ensures adherence to parliamentary procedures and prevents disruptions during sessions.
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** Articles 93 and 94 of the Indian Constitution pertain to the election and duties of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms emotes a play through dancing in which the song is customarily in Manipravala language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical dance form of Kerala, India, known for its graceful movements and emotive storytelling.
 
• The songs performed in Mohiniattam are traditionally composed in the **Manipravala language**, which is a mix of Malayalam and Sanskrit.
 
• This dance form primarily depicts themes of love and devotion, often based on stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• Mohiniattam is characterized by slow, rhythmic movements and unique costumes featuring white sarees with golden borders.
 
• The term "Mohiniattam" translates to "dance of the enchantress," referring to Mohini, a mythical avatar of Lord Vishnu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipravala Language:** A blend of Malayalam and Sanskrit, commonly used in classical literature and dance compositions in Kerala.
 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:** India has eight classical dance forms recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniattam, Sattriya, and Manipuri.
 
• **Kerala's Cultural Heritage:** Kerala is renowned for its rich traditions in classical dance, music, and theater, with Mohiniattam being a significant part of its artistic legacy.
 
• **Costume and Jewelry:** Mohiniattam dancers wear traditional white attire with golden borders, along with elegant jewelry and floral hair adornments.
 
• **Training and Performance:** Mohiniattam requires years of rigorous training in classical music, dance techniques, and expressive gestures (Abhinaya) to master its nuances.

questions.question: The Home Rule League Movement of Bal Gangadhar Tilak had its base across Karnataka and Maharashtra, but excluding which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Home Rule League Movement was started by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** in April 1916 and had its base in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
 
• Tilak’s league aimed at promoting self-governance and instilling nationalist sentiment among Indians through public meetings, campaigns, and outreach efforts.
 
• The movement, though spread across Maharashtra and Karnataka, specifically excluded **Bombay** from its base of operations.
 
• The exclusion of Bombay was due to Tilak’s strategic focus on regions where nationalist sentiment was robust and the likelihood of mass mobilization higher.
 
• Tilak’s Home Rule League primarily focused on rural and semi-urban areas to spread political awareness among the masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Home Rule League Movement:**

 
 
• It was inspired by the Irish Home Rule Movement and aimed at gaining self-rule within the British Empire.
 
• Two Home Rule Leagues operated simultaneously—one led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and the other by Annie Besant.
 
• Annie Besant’s league covered regions like Madras, Bombay, and parts of northern India.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**
 
 
• Known as the "Father of Indian Unrest," Tilak was a prominent freedom fighter and social reformer.
 
• He popularized the slogan "**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**."
 
• Tilak’s efforts were instrumental in mobilizing the masses for India’s independence struggle.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Home Rule Movement:**
 
 
• It significantly contributed to the rise of nationalist sentiment and political consciousness among Indians.
 
• It laid the foundation for future mass movements like the Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience movements.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Movement:**
 
 
• The Home Rule Movement began to decline by 1919 following the introduction of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms and the Rowlatt Act agitation.
 
• Many leaders shifted focus to broader struggles for complete independence.

questions.question: Which of the following is the residential place of Buddhist priests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vihara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vihara** is the term used for monasteries or residential places where Buddhist monks and priests reside.
 
• These structures were primarily built near forests or secluded areas to ensure a tranquil environment for meditation and study.
 
• Viharas were initially used as temporary shelters during the rainy season but evolved into permanent monasteries over time.
 
• Architecturally, viharas often included a central courtyard surrounded by residential cells for monks and communal spaces for prayer and learning.
 
• They played a significant role in spreading Buddhist teachings and served as centers of education and community activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa:** A dome-shaped structure that serves as a Buddhist shrine, primarily used for meditation and housing relics of Buddha or other revered figures.
 
• **Stambha:** Pillars or columns often inscribed with edicts and teachings of Emperor Ashoka, symbolizing the spread of Buddhism.
 
• **Chaitya:** A prayer hall or assembly hall with a stupa at its center, used for congregational worship and meditation.
 
• **Buddhist Monastic Life:** Monks followed strict disciplinary codes (Vinaya), and Viharas provided an environment for spiritual growth, study, and communal living.
 
• **Spread of Buddhism:** Monasteries like Viharas became centers of learning and played a pivotal role in the dissemination of Buddhist philosophy across Asia.

questions.question: Which festival commemorates the death of Hussain Ibn Ali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muharram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muharram** is one of the four sacred months in the Islamic calendar and marks the beginning of the new Islamic year.
 
• It commemorates the martyrdom of **Imam Hussain Ibn Ali**, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, in the Battle of Karbala in 680 CE.
 
• The 10th day of Muharram, known as **Ashura**, holds special significance for Muslims worldwide.
 
• Shia Muslims observe Muharram as a period of mourning, with processions, recitations, and re-enactments of the events of Karbala.
 
• Sunni Muslims may observe fasting on Ashura to commemorate the day Prophet Musa (Moses) and his followers were saved from Pharaoh’s tyranny.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Karbala:** The battle occurred in Karbala (modern-day Iraq) on 10th Muharram 61 AH (680 CE) where Imam Hussain and his followers were killed by the army of Yazid I.
 
• **Ashura Practices:** Shia Muslims express grief through chest-beating (matam), mourning processions, and reciting elegies, while Sunni Muslims may fast on this day.
 
• **Islamic Calendar:** Muharram is the first month of the Hijri calendar, which is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 months.
 
• **Significance of Ashura:** Apart from the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, Ashura is also linked to events such as the Exodus of Israelites and the repentance of Prophet Yunus (Jonah).
 
• **Global Observance:** Muharram is observed differently across the Muslim world, with traditions varying between Shia and Sunni communities.

questions.question: The Mawsynram receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world. It is located in which hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mawsynram**, located in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, is the wettest place on Earth.
 
• It receives an average annual rainfall of around **11,871 millimeters** (467.4 inches).
 
• Mawsynram is situated in the **Khasi Hills**, one of the three major hill ranges in Meghalaya.
 
• The high rainfall is attributed to the region's unique topography and its proximity to the **Bay of Bengal**, leading to heavy monsoonal clouds being trapped by the hills.
 
• The region's dense vegetation and terrain play a critical role in sustaining its ecological balance despite the heavy rainfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Hills:**

 
 
• The Khasi Hills are part of the Meghalaya Plateau, which is an extension of the Indian Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The hills are named after the Khasi tribe, one of the indigenous tribes of Meghalaya.
 
• Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, is also located in the Khasi Hills region.
 
 
 
• **Rainfall Factors in Mawsynram:**
 
 
• The topography of the Khasi Hills forces moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal to ascend, leading to heavy orographic rainfall.
 
• The monsoon winds deposit large quantities of rain in the region, particularly during the summer monsoon season (June to September).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Cherrapunji:**
 
 
• Cherrapunji, also in the Khasi Hills, was earlier considered the wettest place on Earth but is now surpassed by Mawsynram in terms of average annual rainfall.
 
• Both locations experience similar climatic conditions, with heavy monsoonal rains and short dry periods.
 
 
 
• **Ecological and Cultural Impact:**
 
 
• The heavy rainfall supports lush greenery, including dense forests and grasslands, crucial for biodiversity.
 
• Traditional Khasi architecture and lifestyle in the region are adapted to withstand the heavy rains.

questions.question: Which of the following national income aggregates is generally recognised as National Income of a country?

options.text: Net National Product at Market Prices
Net National Product at Factor Cost
Gross National Product at Market Prices
Gross Domestic Product at Factor Cost

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net National Product at Factor Cost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost, also referred to as National Income, is the aggregate value of all goods and services produced within a country after accounting for depreciation and taxes.
 
• It is derived by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from Gross National Product (GNP) at Factor Cost.
 
• Unlike market prices, factor cost excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies, making it a more accurate measure of the income earned by factors of production.
 
• NNP at Factor Cost is widely used by governments and economists to assess the economic performance and income distribution of a nation.
 
• This measurement reflects the total earnings of a country's residents from the production of goods and services during a specific time period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP):**

 
 
• GNP refers to the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents in a given period, regardless of where the production takes place.
 
• It includes income earned by nationals working abroad but excludes income earned by foreigners within the country.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP):**
 
 
• NNP is GNP adjusted for depreciation, which accounts for the wear and tear of capital assets used in production.
 
• It represents the actual addition to a country's stock of wealth during a year.
 
 
 
• **Factor Cost vs. Market Prices:**
 
 
• Factor Cost accounts for the cost of production, including wages, rent, interest, and profits, but excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies.
 
• Market Prices, on the other hand, include indirect taxes and exclude subsidies, reflecting the price paid by consumers.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation:**
 
 
• Depreciation, also known as consumption of fixed capital, refers to the reduction in the value of assets due to wear and tear over time.
 
• It is subtracted from GNP to calculate NNP.
 
 
 
• **Importance of NNP at Factor Cost:**
 
 
• It serves as a comprehensive indicator of a nation's economic health and income distribution.
 
• It helps policymakers in planning and implementing economic policies aimed at improving living standards.

questions.question: From which state in India did the legendary volleyball player Jimmy George hail?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jimmy George, hailed as one of India’s greatest volleyball players, was born in **Kerala**.
 
• He was born in **Mavelikkara, Alappuzha District**, Kerala on March 8, 1955.
 
• Jimmy George was the first Indian volleyball player to play professionally overseas, representing clubs in Italy.
 
• He was awarded the **Arjuna Award** in 1976 for his exceptional contributions to Indian volleyball.
 
• Jimmy George passed away in a tragic car accident in **Italy** in 1987, leaving behind a legacy as a pioneer in Indian volleyball.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volleyball in India:**

 
 
• Volleyball is a popular sport in India, governed by the **Volleyball Federation of India (VFI)**.
 
• India has consistently performed well in volleyball tournaments in Asia, particularly in the **Asian Games**.
 
• The sport gained significant recognition due to players like Jimmy George.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award:**
 
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is one of India's highest sporting honors, established in 1961.
 
• It recognizes outstanding achievements in national sports and is awarded by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• Jimmy George received the award for his exceptional contributions to volleyball in India.
 
 
 
• **Professional Volleyball Career:**
 
 
• Jimmy George represented **India** in several international volleyball tournaments, including the Asian Games.
 
• He played professionally for **Italian clubs**, such as Coletto Club and Treviso, which marked a historic milestone for Indian volleyball.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Contribution to Sports:**
 
 
• Kerala is renowned for producing exceptional athletes across various sports, including volleyball, athletics, and cricket.
 
• Other notable athletes from Kerala include **P.T. Usha** (track and field) and **Sreesanth** (cricket).
 
• Sports culture in Kerala is deeply rooted, with strong emphasis on nurturing talent at the grassroots level.

questions.question: Who among the following has been appointed as the new Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in June 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Janardan Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Janardan Prasad** was appointed as the new Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in June 2023.
 
• He succeeded the previous Director General to lead GSI, which is a premier Indian organization for geological studies and exploration.
 
• As the head of GSI, he is responsible for providing leadership in areas such as mineral exploration, geological mapping, and geo-scientific research.
 
• The Geological Survey of India, under the Ministry of Mines, plays a critical role in supporting sustainable resource development in the country.
 
• The appointment of Janardan Prasad marks a significant step in advancing India’s geological and mineral exploration initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geological Survey of India (GSI):**

 
 
• Established in 1851, it is one of the oldest scientific institutions in India.
 
• Its primary objective is the exploration and assessment of mineral resources, and it plays a key role in geoscientific research.
 
• GSI also contributes to disaster management by providing geological expertise in areas prone to earthquakes and landslides.
 
 
 
• **Functions of GSI:**
 
 
• Conducting geological surveys and investigations across the nation.
 
• Mapping mineral resources and assessing their economic potential.
 
• Providing technical inputs for mining activities and environmental management.
 
 
 
• **India’s Mineral Resources:**
 
 
• India is rich in mineral resources such as coal, iron ore, bauxite, and mica.
 
• The country ranks among the top producers of several minerals globally.
 
• Sustainable mining practices are a key focus area for economic growth and environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Geological Studies:**
 
 
• Geology helps in understanding earth processes, natural disasters, and resource distribution.
 
• It plays a vital role in infrastructure development, water resource management, and energy exploration.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II was the famous ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the most prominent rulers of the **Chalukya dynasty**, which ruled large parts of southern and central India.
 
• He reigned during the early 7th century CE (circa 610-642 CE) and is best known for his military conquests and administrative capabilities.
 
• Pulakeshin II successfully repelled the northward expansion of **Harsha**, the ruler of Kannauj, in a significant battle near the Narmada River.
 
• He expanded the Chalukya Empire significantly, establishing control over Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh regions.
 
• The **Aihole inscription**, composed by his court poet Ravikirti, provides detailed accounts of his conquests and achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were divided into three branches: the Early Chalukyas (Badami Chalukyas), the Western Chalukyas, and the Eastern Chalukyas.
 
• They made significant contributions to art, architecture, and administration, including iconic temples at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription:**
 
 
• It is a Sanskrit inscription in Kannada script that details Pulakeshin II's victories and his valor.
 
• The inscription also describes Pulakeshin II as a great patron of culture and a skilled administrator.
 
 
 
• **Harsha:**
 
 
• He was a powerful ruler of northern India during the 7th century, and his empire extended across much of the Gangetic plain.
 
• His defeat by Pulakeshin II marked the southern boundary of his empire.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal Temples:**
 
 
• Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases the architectural brilliance of the Chalukyas under Pulakeshin II's reign.
 
• These temples represent a fusion of Dravidian and Nagara architectural styles.

questions.question: For the development of agriculture, a new department, Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi was established by which of the following Sultans of Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** was a special department established by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq for the development of agriculture.
 
• This department was responsible for improving agricultural practices and increasing crop production by providing state support to farmers.
 
• Muhammad Bin Tughlaq focused on expanding cultivation by introducing new irrigation systems and granting loans to farmers.
 
• The initiative aimed to improve food security and stabilize the economy during his reign.
 
• Despite ambitious efforts, many of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq's agricultural reforms faced challenges due to poor implementation and lack of local support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq:** He ruled from 1325 to 1351 and was known for his ambitious projects and administrative innovations.
 
• **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi:** This department was specifically created to oversee agricultural reforms and ensure efficient administration in rural areas.
 
• **Irrigation Systems:** Muhammad Bin Tughlaq introduced canal irrigation and other water management techniques to support agriculture.
 
• **Agricultural Loans:** Loans were provided to farmers under state supervision to encourage cultivation of barren lands.
 
• Many reforms failed due to excessive taxation, lack of proper implementation, and resistance from farmers.
